tasks.short: Grade class assignments and papers against her rubric.

steps.what: Read the class assignment brief and rubric.
Read the students papers for these assignments.
Look up stored citation rules for papers.
Draft rubric comments that quote the papers.

loop.input: One student paper plus her rubric sentences for this assignment.
loop.output: One draft comment per rubric item, each with a quoted passage from that paper.
loop.check: The comment matches that rubric claim, and the quote appears in the paper, rather than matching only an identifier or a score.
loop.stop: One pass. An item with no quote is left unmarked and is not rewritten.
loop.why_not_simpler: A field copy of the rubric sentence cannot write the comment against this paper.

steps.what: Evaluate and grade the students papers.
Copy the approved grade into the result register.

tasks.design: A lookup on the {LMS} applies citation-rule fields the instructional coordinator keeps in the {DOCS}, and a bounded loop drafts one quoted rubric comment per item, stopping when an item has no quote. The communications teacher evaluates and grades every paper, and the course gradebook entry is that same decision. A separate gated step copies only that approved snapshot into the official student-record register ({OTHER}).
tasks.previous_blocker: A comment has to quote a passage in that paper, and the grade is the examiner's decision, so a stored form could not finish the task.
tasks.enabler_now: Rubric sentences and citation rules can be stored as fields, and the official register is already a second entry she re-keys by hand.
tasks.still_hard: Papers where a rubric item has no quotable passage, and the duty to set the grade, stay with her.
tasks.human_edge: She judges whether the quoted passage meets the rubric claim, and she sets every grade.
tasks.altitude: Her week still includes every paper and every grade. A first comment arrives with a quote when the fields exist. She gains no right to let a model set the result.

reach.task: Maintain rubric-item sentences and citation-rule fields for communications papers.
reach.learn: Which rubric items she leaves unmarked because the paper has no quote.

evidence.claim: FeedbackFruits gives formative feedback on writing criteria such as citation style, and teachers edit the criteria.
Brightspace Lumi drafts text and rubric feedback from the instructor's notes.
At Radboud, grades entered in Brightspace must also be published in OSIRIS, so the same result is entered in a second register.
Annex III point 3 covers evaluating learning outcomes, and AI grading duties apply from 2 December 2027.
A grade set solely by a model is likely a GDPR article 22 decision.
Under WHW 7.12c, examiners appointed by the examination board set the result.
Emotion inference in education is banned. The comment draft quotes a passage and does not infer emotion.
The communications teacher still reads the paper and sets the grade. The loop only proposes a comment tied to a quote.

assumptions: The focal role is the communications teacher. Her boundary on this task is reading the assignment, reading the papers, and setting each grade. Fraud sanctions stay with the examination board and are not part of this task.

Citation-rule fields are style name and required elements. Rubric-item fields are the claim sentence. The instructional coordinator produces both. If those fields are absent, the lookup and the comment draft do not run, and she checks citations while she reads and grades.

The official student-record register is a second system, named here as {OTHER}. The registry clerk keeps its field map: student identifier, course code, approved grade, result date. The course gradebook entry of the decision she just made stays inside s5 and is not a separate save.
Focal upkeep is zero. She does not maintain the citation rules, the rubric items, or the register map.
unknowns: Whether this faculty re-keys the course grade into a second official register.
Whether rubric items and citation rules are stored as fields or only as a narrative document.
research_questions: How many minutes does the second register entry take on a typical assignment, once the course grade is already set?

already_counted.description: Reading each paper, editing comments, setting the grade, and recording that decision in the course gradebook already sit in s5.

incremental.description: Focal upkeep for field maps. Justified as zero in assumptions, because she does not keep those lists.
The instructional coordinator maintains rubric-item sentences and citation-rule fields.
The registry clerk maintains the result-register field map used by the copy.

approvals.approved_version: The course grade and comment snapshot the communications teacher recorded for each student in s5. Any later edit voids this approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Where the rubric is only narrative, the comment draft does not run, and a typical second register leaves the copy, about 6. Where rubric fields exist she still rewrites many comments, so the high stays at 18, under the 28 that also counts the lookup and the draft.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare syllabi, homework assignments and handouts for the course.

steps.what: Read stored outcomes to prepare course materials.
Decide the homework and handouts this course needs.
Draft syllabi, homework assignments and handouts.

loop.input: Stored outcome sentences, timetable dates, and her prior handout wording.
loop.output: Draft syllabi, homework assignments and handouts for this sitting.
loop.check: Each paragraph uses only those outcome sentences, dates and her prior wording, and adds no new outcome.
loop.stop: One pass. A gap with no stored sentence is left blank and is not filled in.
loop.why_not_simpler: Copying the dates cannot write the assignment paragraph.

steps.what: Rewrite the syllabi and homework in her words.
Publish the approved course materials.

tasks.design: She reads outcome sentences and dates from the {DOCS} and the {CALENDAR}, decides the homework and handouts, and a bounded loop drafts syllabi, homework assignments and handouts from those fields and her prior wording. She rewrites the final text. A separate gated step publishes that approved version to students on the {LMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: The homework paragraph has to be written for this sitting, so a copy of last year's file was not the task.
tasks.enabler_now: Outcome sentences, sitting dates and her prior wording can be stored, and the student course page is a real upload from the document she signs.
tasks.still_hard: She still rewrites the voice of the syllabi and the homework before students see them.
tasks.human_edge: She decides what this sitting needs and signs the wording students will read.
tasks.altitude: She still chooses the homework and handouts and still signs the syllabi. The first draft is faster when outcome sentences are stored. Students still see only the version she rewrote.

reach.task: Maintain the outcome-sentence list and sitting dates for the course.
reach.learn: Which outcome sentences she rewrote before the materials were published.

evidence.claim: Drafting syllabi and handouts is not covered by the annex III duty on evaluating learning outcomes, nor by the grading and proctoring duties that apply from 2 December 2027.
Dates and outcome sentences can be copied, but the homework paragraph has to be written, so she rewrites the draft before it is published.

assumptions: The focal role is the communications teacher. She decides what this sitting needs, rewrites the materials, and publishes the version she signed.

Outcome fields are the outcome sentence and the sitting date. Prior handout wording is her earlier paragraph. The programme lead produces the outcome-sentence list. If the outcomes are only a narrative document, the draft does not run and she writes the materials herself. She still publishes them.
Publishing puts the approved document on the student course page in the {LMS}. That is a release to students, not a save back into the {DOCS}.
Focal upkeep is zero. She does not maintain the outcome-sentence list.
unknowns: Whether learning outcomes at this faculty are stored as separate sentences with dates, or only inside last year's syllabi.
research_questions: How often does she rewrite a drafted homework paragraph before she is willing to publish it?

already_counted.description: Rewriting the syllabi and homework in her own words, which is the version later published, already sits in s4.

incremental.description: Focal upkeep for the outcome list. Justified as zero in assumptions.
The programme lead maintains the outcome-sentence list and sitting dates.

approvals.approved_version: The final syllabi, homework assignments and handouts wording the communications teacher signed in s4. Any later edit voids this approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When outcomes are only narrative, the draft does not run and only the upload to the student course page remains, about 6. With stored outcomes she still rewrites most paragraphs, so the high is 22, under the 32 that also counts the draft.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Initiate, facilitate and moderate classroom discussions.

steps.what: Read the prompt for the classroom discussions.
Show the stored prompt for classroom discussions.
Initiate the classroom discussions with that prompt.
Facilitate and moderate the classroom discussions.
Note questions the classroom discussions left open.

tasks.design: If the discussion prompt is already a stored field on the approved materials, the {LMS} shows it. She still initiates, facilitates and moderates the classroom discussions in the room, and she notes questions left open. The room stays hers.
tasks.previous_blocker: The discussion is spoken with the students in the room, so there is no record that can stand in for it.
tasks.enabler_now: A prompt she already approved with the course materials can be stored as a field and shown at the start of the session.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to read the room, invite the quiet students, and stop a line of talk that is not the point.
tasks.human_edge: She initiates, facilitates and moderates the live discussion. A stored prompt does not do that.
tasks.altitude: Her week in the classroom does not change. She may spend a little less time hunting the prompt she already wrote. She still runs the discussion.

reach.task: Keep the discussion prompt as a field on the approved course materials.
reach.learn: Which prompts she still had to replace once the class was in the room.

evidence.claim: Live facilitation of a classroom discussion is spoken work in the room and is not a records step.

assumptions: The focal role is the communications teacher. She initiates, facilitates and moderates the discussion in the room. Spoken talk with students is not a versioned send, so those steps are ungated.
The stored prompt is a field already kept with the approved course materials. If that field is absent, the show step does not run and she uses the prompt she just read. This task adds no new list.
Focal upkeep is zero. No one keeps a separate discussion-prompt list for this task.
unknowns: Whether the discussion prompt is already a field on the approved materials, or only a line in her own notes.
research_questions: On a morning when the course page is already open, how long does finding the prompt actually take?

already_counted.description: Initiating and moderating the classroom discussion in the room is unchanged and already sits in s3 and s4.

incremental.description: Focal upkeep for a prompt list. Justified as zero in assumptions, because no new list is kept.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A spoken plan with no stored prompt saves nothing, so the low is 0. A stored field saves only the hunt for the prompt, and a morning with the page already open saves less, so the high is 3, under the 4 for that lookup.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compile, administer and grade examinations, or assign that work.

steps.what: Compile the examinations or assign them to others.
Pull tagged closed items for the examinations.
Administer the examinations in the room.
Mark closed items on the examinations.
Group similar short answers on the examinations.

loop.input: Short answers on the examinations plus the rubric bands she set on the key.
loop.output: A proposed group of similar answers and a proposed rubric band for that group.
loop.check: The answers in the group match each other in wording, and the band matches the rubric, rather than matching an answer identifier.
loop.stop: One pass. A group with high disagreement is left unmarked for her to grade.
loop.why_not_simpler: A key match on closed options cannot group open wording.

steps.what: Grade the examinations and confirm each mark.
Copy approved examination grades to the register.

tasks.design: She compiles the examinations and may assign marking to a teaching assistant. The {LMS} pulls tagged closed items and marks them against the key she set, and a bounded loop groups similar short answers, leaving high disagreement unmarked. She grades and confirms every mark in the course record, then a separate gated step copies that approved snapshot into the official student-record register ({OTHER}).
tasks.previous_blocker: Open answers are not a key match, and the result is the examiner's decision, so closed-item scoring alone never finished the examination.
tasks.enabler_now: An item bank can store the correct option and a topic tag, and similar short answers can be grouped for one look before she confirms the mark.
tasks.still_hard: She still administers the examination in the room, still reads the open answers, and still sets every result.
tasks.human_edge: She chooses the items, confirms every mark, and sets the examination result. The examination board, not she, sanctions fraud.
tasks.altitude: She still compiles the paper, still sits the examination, and still confirms every mark. Closed items and grouped short answers arrive as drafts. She gains no right to skip an open answer.

reach.task: Mark the closed items the communications teacher assigns, after she confirms the batch.
reach.learn: A closed-item mark waits for her confirmation before it is a result.

evidence.claim: Ans auto-marks closed questions and splits open answers among markers, and the descriptions do not list a model for that marking.
Gradescope groups similar answers so each group can be graded once. The physics time estimate in that source is not used as this task's saving.
At Radboud, grades entered in Brightspace must also be published in OSIRIS, so an examination result is entered again in the official register.
Under WHW 7.12c the examiner sets the result, and under 7.12b only the examination board sanctions fraud.
Annex III point 3 covers evaluating learning outcomes, and AI grading duties apply from 2 December 2027.
A grade set solely by a model is likely a GDPR article 22 decision.
The inspectorate report on examination boards treats generative tools as a threat to test validity, so the examiner still confirms each mark.
A system that can monitor staff, such as a per-examiner marking dashboard, needs works-council consent under WOR 27. This design has no such dashboard.
Closed-item marking against a stored key is a comparison. Open answers still need the examiner to confirm the mark. Essay comment drafting is a different task and is not counted here.

assumptions: The focal role is the communications teacher. She compiles the examination, administers it in the room, and confirms every mark. Assigning marking to a teaching assistant is a colleague handoff inside s1. The assistant's own hours are not in this baseline. She does not file fraud; the examination board sanctions it.

Item-bank fields are item text, correct option, topic tag and item type. The instructional coordinator produces them. Closed items are marked only against the key she set in s1. Untagged or open items are not auto-marked. The grouping loop proposes a band and leaves high disagreement unmarked.

The course record of the decision she confirms stays inside s6. The copy into the official student-record register ({OTHER}) is a second entry. The registry clerk keeps that field map. If this faculty has no second register, the copy step is not built.

Comment drafting on class papers is a different task and is not counted again here. Focal upkeep is zero. She does not maintain the item-bank tags or the register map. No per-examiner marking dashboard is included, so the works-council consent for staff monitoring is not triggered by this design.
unknowns: What share of a typical examination is closed items with a stored correct option.
Whether this faculty re-keys examination results into a second official register.
research_questions: On a mixed paper, how many short answers fall into a group she accepts unchanged?

already_counted.description: Confirming each examination grade, including the course record of that decision, already sits in s6.

incremental.description: Focal upkeep for the item bank and the register map. Justified as zero in assumptions.
The instructional coordinator maintains item-bank fields: correct option, topic tag and item type.
The registry clerk maintains the result-register field map for examination results.

approvals.approved_version: The examination grade snapshot the communications teacher confirmed for each student in s6. Any later edit voids this approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: An essay-only examination with a second register leaves about the copy, 6. A mixed paper with a tagged bank and a second register still leaves her reading every open answer, so the high is 16, under the 26 that also counts the pull, the closed marks and the grouping.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: She still grades every paper, still runs the classroom discussion, and still sets every examination result. Draft comments, a materials draft, a stored prompt, closed-item marks and a register copy are the machine steps. She gains no right to let a model set a grade.
skills_to_grow: Judge a quoted passage against the rubric claim before setting the grade.
Rewrite syllabi and homework so they keep only the approved outcome sentences.
Moderate classroom discussions when the stored prompt is a weak opener.
Confirm each examination mark, including a closed item scored from the key.
role.ambitious_version: Once rubric fields and the second register are in place, she uses the comment-draft time on papers where a rubric item had no quote. She still sets every grade, still runs every classroom discussion, and still confirms every examination result.
